newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's cabinet okays stabilization fund.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's cabinet okays stabilization fund.

text.p: Venezuela's Cabinet approved Wednesday the creation of a macroeconomic stabilization fund designed to buffer the oil-rich country in times of low international oil prices, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
"We believe this decision is one of the most important in changing the country's development strategy and improving the management of public finances," Matos told reporters.

Matos said the fund would stockpile windfall revenues when international oil prices rise, and then be drawn down as oil prices fall. The revenue smoothing would cushion the budget in lean years, he added.
The bill is due to be sent to congress in the next few days.

Last year, Venezuela received some $3 billion in windfall oil revenues. State-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) president Luis Giusti said Tuesday the government had so far saved some $1.6 billion in a special off-budget account.
